## The Monetarist Theory is attributed to Milton Friedman, although Marshall and Pigou also made significant contributions to the functional relationship between nominal money stock and the general price level.

1. The key principle of this theory is that in a monetary economy, money supply growth is the only determinant of inflation.
2. It's based on the quantity theory of money, which holds that inflation is a phenomenon that results only from money supply fluctuations.
3. According to the Keynesian Theory, inflation affects output positively in the short-run and negatively in the long-run.
4. This implies that in an economy where inflation is targeted, low stable inflation is likely to cause a fall in output in the short-run but a rise in output in the long-run.

examples.src: **Its main goal is to protect the kernel against itself from vulnerabilities such as unauthorized kernel modification and privilege escalation. The traditional OS architecture is made up of four major subsystems: hardware controllers, OS kernel, OS services layer, and user applications. It is classified into kernel space, which includes the kernel and the lower part of the OS services layer, and user space, which includes the upper part of the OS services layer and user applications. To apply the downloaded grsecurity patches to the Linux kernel, you need to copy the required directories from the Ubuntu kernel overlay directory to the correct ubuntu-package directory using the 'cp' command. Then, you need to patch the kernel using the 'patch' command. To configure the kernel using the 'ncurses' interface, you can use the 'make menuconfig' command. The paradigm shift in OS development from distributed environment to OS security since the late 1990s highlights the increasing importance of security in operating system design. The Convoluted Kernel contributes to this shift by providing a novel kernel architecture designed to protect the kernel against itself from vulnerabilities such as unauthorized kernel modification and privilege escalation.**

examples.src: In the year two thousand and twenty-three, Gina started a project that will help young men and young women who want to be "professional players" in various sports. *Many people think it is not hard to help someone, but Gina's project makes a difference.* She put all her time and her money into that work. In the "documentary" they made about her work, we saw how her "dedication" crosses all boundaries. She went to "training camps" that are in Nigeria, Ghana, and many places, and it is there she put her mind on young women who have "potential" but don't have "resources." As the matter is, many people want to talk but with Gina, it is her work that talks. In her work, she put Fuji rhythm and the "cultural essence" that is in Yoruba sound into that sport, and it will make the young women know that their "roots" can be proof in foreign lands. People who investigated that work said, "Gina's impact transcends geographical boundaries." It is not just understanding why she did that, but she wants to make "aspiring players" know they have a "platform" that will make them go high. If we look, people like Gina are the first to make the "industry" expand to places where no one else was. If you go look at her history, you will see it is not only her, but her "legacy" and the work she left behind that will stay for many people. It is a "standard" that will make others also have the mind to work hard for their "goals."
examples.ref: Wɔ afe mpem mmienu ne aduonu mmiensa no mu, Gina hyɛɛ dwumadie bi a ɛbɛboa mmeranteɛ ne mmabaa a wɔpɛ sɛ wɔyɛ "professional players" wɔ agodie ahorow mu. *Nnipa pii susuw sɛ ɛnyɛ den sɛ wobɛboa obi, nanso Gina dwumadie no di nsonsonoeɛ.* Ɔde ne berɛ ne ne sika nyinaa hyɛɛ saa dwuma no mu. Wɔ "documentary" a wɔyɛɛ faa n'adwuma no ho no, yɛhuu sɛdeɛ ne "dedication" no twa hyeɛ nyinaa. Ɔkɔɔ "training camps" a ɛwɔ Nigeria, Ghana, ne mmeaeɛ pii, na ɛhɔ na ɔde n'adwene hyɛɛ mmabaa a wɔwɔ "potential" nanso wɔnni "resources" no so. Sɛdeɛ asɛm no te no, nnipa pii pɛ sɛ wɔkasa nanso Gina deɛ, n'adwuma na ɛkasa. Wɔ ne dwumadie mu no, ɔde Fuji rhythm ne "cultural essence" a ɛwɔ Yoruba nnyigyeɛ mu no hyɛɛ saa agodie no mu, na ɛbɛma mmabaa no ahu sɛ wɔn "roots" no bɛtumi ayɛ adanseɛ wɔ amanɔne. Sɛ wose wohwɛ n'abakɔsɛm a, wobehu sɛ ɛnyɛ ɔno nkutoo, na mmom ne "legacy" ne adwuma a ɔgyaa hɔ na ɛbɛtena hɔ ama nnipa dodoɔ. Ɛyɛ "standard" bi a ɛbɛma afoforɔ nso adwenem ayɛ wɔn sɛ wɔbɛbɔ mmɔden ama wɔn "goals".

examples.src: Yes, of course. There's been significant research on antiretroviral therapy in Ghana. For instance, a study published in the International Conference on AIDS in two thousand and four found that anaemia is a common issue among patients accessing antiretroviral therapy in Ghana. The study, led by Torpey et al., highlighted the need for close monitoring of patients on antiretroviral therapy to manage anaemia and other side effects. Yes, that's correct. Antiretroviral therapy has been associated with liver and kidney toxicity. A study published in the Journal of the American Medical Association in two thousand found that hepatitis C or B virus infection can increase the risk of hepatotoxicity associated with antiretroviral therapy. Additionally, research has shown that certain antiretroviral drugs, such as tenofovir, can affect kidney function and increase the risk of kidney disease. Yes, that's correct. Research has shown that some antiretroviral drugs, such as TMCtwo hundred and seventy-eight hectaresve a higher genetic barrier and a more robust resistance profile than first-generation non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). *This means that they are less likely to lead to the development of resistance mutations.* **A study published in Nature Medicine in two thousand and eight found that the dose-response curve slope sets class-specific limits on the inhibitory potential of anti-HIV drugs, which can help guide the development of more effective antiretroviral therapies.** Yes, that's correct. Research has shown that certain antiretroviral drugs, such as tenofovir and abacavir, can affect bone density and increase the risk of osteoporosis. A study published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in two thousand and nine found that changes in bone density and turnover were observed in patients taking abacavir-lamivudine versus tenofovir-emtricitabine in the ASSERT study. This highlights the need for close monitoring of bone health in patients on long-term antiretroviral therapy.
examples.ref: aane saa ara. Wɔayɛ nhwehwɛmu a ɛho hia wɔ nnuru a wɔde kum ɔyare mmoawa ho wɔ Ghana. Sɛ nhwɛso no, nhwehwɛmu bi a wotintimii wɔ afe 2004 mu wɔ Amanaman Ntam AIDS Nhyiam ase kyerɛe sɛ mogya a ɛtɔ kɔ nipadua mu yɛ ɔhaw a ɛtaa ba ayarefo a wɔde nnuru a ekum ɔyare mmoawa ma wɔ Ghana no mu. Nhwehwɛmu a Thorpe ne ne mfɛfo dii anim no kyerɛe sɛ ɛho hia sɛ wɔhwɛ ayarefo a wɔde nnuru a ekum ɔyare mmoawa di dwuma no so yiye na ama wɔatumi asiw mogya a ɛtɔ kɔ mogya mu ne nea efi mu ba afoforo ano. Yiw, ɛno teɛ. Wɔde nnuru a ekum ɔyare mmoawa a wɔde sa yare no abata mmerɛbo ne asaabo mu awuduru ho. Mfe mpem abien nhwehwɛmu bi a wotintimii wɔ Journal of the American Medical Association mu no daa no adi sɛ hepatitis C anaa B mmoawa a wɔde obi ba no ma asiane a ɛwɔ hɔ sɛ obi benya hepatitis awuduru a ɛbata aduru a wɔde kum ɔyare mmoawa ho no yɛ kɛse. Nea ɛka ho no, nhwehwɛmu ahorow ada no adi sɛ nnuru bi a wɔde ko tia HIV te sɛ tenofovir betumi aka asaabo dwumadi na ama asiane a ɛwɔ hɔ sɛ obi benya asaabo mu yare no ayɛ kɛse. Yiw, ɛno teɛ. Nhwehwɛmu ahorow ada no adi sɛ nnuru bi a ekum ɔyare mmoawa te sɛ TMC 278 ha no wɔ awosu mu ahoɔden a ɛko tia nyarewa kɛse na ɛko tia nyarewa a emu yɛ den sen awo ntoatoaso a edi kan a ɛnyɛ nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). *Eyi kyerɛ sɛ ɛnyɛ den koraa sɛ ɛbɛma nkwaadɔm mu nsakrae a ɛko tia nyarewa no aba.* **Nhwehwɛmu bi a wotintimii wɔ Nature Medicine mu wɔ afe 2008 mu no kyerɛe sɛ dose-response curve no de anohyeto ahorow a ɛfa adesuakuw pɔtee bi ho wɔ tumi a nnuru a ekum HIV tumi siw ano no so, na ɛboa ma wɔyɛ nnuru a etu mpɔn a wɔde ko tia HIV.** Yiw, ɛno teɛ. Nhwehwɛmu ahorow ada no adi sɛ nnuru bi a ekum ɔyare mmoawa te sɛ tenofovir ne abacavir betumi aka nnompe a ɛyɛ den na ama nnompe mu yare ayɛ kɛse. Sɛnea nhwehwɛmu bi a wotintimii wɔ Clinical Infectious Diseases mu wɔ afe 2009 mu kyerɛ no, wohuu nsakrae wɔ nnompe ahoɔden ne nsakrae mu wɔ ayarefo a wɔde abacavir-lamivudine vs tenofovir-emtricitabine maa wɔn wɔ ASSERT nhwehwɛmu no mu no mu. Eyi si hia a ɛho hia sɛ wɔhwɛ nnompe akwahosan so yiye wɔ ayarefo a wɔde nnuru a ekum ɔyare mmoawa a ɛtra hɔ kyɛ di dwuma no so dua.
examples.dict: Yiw, adesua bi wɔ hɔ a wɔayɛ ho nhwehwɛmu kɛseɛ wɔ asramma ayaresa ho wɔ Ghana. examples.src: The Governor of the Central Bank acknowledged the concerns raised by economic analysts, but emphasized that the MPC had carefully evaluated the economy and considered all the facts on the ground before making the decision to reduce the policy rate. He also stated that the Central Bank is monitoring the situation closely and will respond appropriately if there are any negative impacts on inflation. Commercial banks in Ghana have been slow to adjust their base rates despite the reduction in the policy rate. Currently, policy rates hover between thirty percent and thirty-three percent on average, which is considered too high by the business community. However, the Governor of the Central Bank is optimistic that banks will eventually reduce their base rates to reflect the downward trend of the policy rate. Professor Stephen Adei believes that the difference between the policy rate and commercial banks' base rates is not too wide, and that the government should introduce a policy to compel commercial banks to drive their interest rates down each time the Central Bank reduces the policy rate. *He also suggests that the government should define a framework to guide the rates commercial banks charge, as the current liberal market economy allows banks to charge high interest rates.*

examples.src: **Patrick was a young man who had earned his degree, and everyone hoped he would progress in his career, but death has claimed him. According to reports, Patrick’s sudden death has left his friends and family devastated. It is heartbreaking that someone with such promise, having completed his education, should die in this manner. Today, the entire KNUST community is quiet, but it is a silence of mourning, not of peace. People are asking themselves, "What happened to Patrick?" He was a writer, he was full of hope, and he wanted to support his family. Yet, death heeds no one. Looking at how his friends speak of him, it is clear he was a person who loved others. This story teaches us that life is fleeting; today you are here, tomorrow you are gone. It reminds us all that we must take good care of ourselves. The KNUST community continues to grow and do great work, but this tragedy will forever remain in their hearts. When we speak of Patrick, we do not only speak of his accolades, what he did for the school, or the love he had for his friends. *This death has caused many to reflect on their own lives and ask themselves deep questions.* The sorrow is real, but we all know that death knows no rules. Patrick’s death should not be something that weighs down our hearts; rather, it should encourage us to live our lives well and continue to treat one another with respect while we are still alive. When one departs, they should be someone spoken well of. That is what Patrick has done. Today, we are all praying for his family, and coming together as one family.**

## The falling head permeameter method involves driving an infiltrometer into the soil to a depth of fifteen centimeters and maintaining a constant head of water, typically five centimeters, from a measuring cylinder.

1. The volume of water used to maintain the constant head is recorded at regular intervals, and the cumulative infiltration amount is plotted as a function of time.
2. The slope of the cumulative infiltration amount taken at different time scales represents the infiltration rate.
3. The data was collected by recording the volume of water used to maintain the constant head at thirty seconds intervals for the first five minutes, sixty seconds intervals for the next five minutes, one hundred and twenty seconds intervals for five minutes, one hundred and eighty seconds intervals for fifteen minutes, and three hundred seconds intervals for thirty minutes.

examples.src: He and another student, Tyron Marhguy, were initially blocked from enrolling at Achimota School in March two thousand and twenty-one due to the school's strict hair policy. However, the Accra High Court ruled on the thirty-first of May in the year twenty twenty-one, that the denial of admission violated their constitutional rights to religious freedom, dignity, and education. Actually, Oheneba didn't attend Achimota School. Instead, he was awarded a scholarship to Ghana International School (GIS) through the Article seventeen Education Trust. The trust was set up by GIS alumnus William Hackman and four other parents to promote access and equality in education. According to the article, Oheneba had a successful experience at GIS. *He graduated from the school, and the CEO, Dr. Mary Asabea Ashun, celebrated his success as a testament to perseverance and progressive thinking.* Dr. Ashun described the decision to admit Oheneba as 'wise and forward-thinking,' and emphasized that GIS remains committed to championing inclusion and access for all students. Oheneba's story highlights the importance of inclusivity and access in education. The fact that GIS was willing to admit him and provide him with a scholarship suggests that there are institutions in Ghana that value diversity and are committed to providing opportunities for all students, regardless of their background or beliefs.
examples.ref: Mfiase no wɔbaraa ɔne osuani foforo, Tyrone Marhgui, sɛ wɔnkyerɛw wɔn din wɔ Achimota Sukuu mu wɔ March 2021 mu esiane sukuu no ti nhwi ho nhyehyɛe a emu yɛ den nti. Nanso gyinaesi a Accra Asɛnnibea Kunini no sii wɔ May 31 tiaa ɔbarima a wadi mfe aduonu biako no bu wɔn hokwan a ɛwɔ mmara mu wɔ nyamesom, nidi ne nhomasua mu ahofadi ho no so. Nokwarem no, Oheneba Achimota ankɔ sukuu. Mmom, wɔmaa no Ahyɛde Dunwɔtwe Akwankyerɛ a wɔde ma Ghana Amanaman Ntam Sukuu (GIS). ህግደፍ እምነት የትሃደርቲ ተግባራሽነት ይኩለ በሊና ለሳዛይማ ምሩቃን ዊሊም ሃክማንላን አራትላ ወጆች የተቋንቋ ነው Sɛnea asɛm no kyerɛ no, Oheneba nyaa adwuma a edi mu wɔ GIS mu. *Owiee sukuu no na CEO, Dr. Mary Asefe Ashum, hyɛɛ no ​​anuonyam sɛ adanseɛ a ɛkyerɛ sɛ ɔyɛɛ ne boasetɔ ne nkɔsoɔ adwene.* Ɔbenfo Ashun Oheneba kaa gyinaesi a wosii sɛ wobegye no atom no ho asɛm sɛ ‘nea nyansa wom na osusuw nneɛma ho kɔ akyiri’ na osii so dua sɛ GIS asi ne bo sɛ ɛbɛka obiara ho na ama asuafo nyinaa anya bi. Oheneba asɛm no si hia a ɛho hia sɛ wɔka obiara ho na wonya nhomasua so dua. Nokwasɛm a ɛyɛ sɛ GIS wɔ ɔpɛ sɛ wobegye no na wɔama no sika a wɔde bɛboa no no kyerɛ sɛ asoɛe ahorow bi wɔ Ghana a wobu ahorow ahorow sɛ ɛsom bo na wɔasi wɔn bo sɛ wɔbɛma hokwan ahorow ama asuafo nyinaa, a wɔn a wofi mu anaa wɔn gyidi mfa ho.
examples.dict: Ɔne osuani foforo Tyrone Marugu dii kan siw no kwan sɛ wɔbɛkyerɛw no din wɔ Achimota Sukuu mu wɔ Ɔbenem mpem mmienu ne aduonu baako. Nanso, Nkran Asɛnnibea Kɛseɛ no buu atɛn wɔ May 31st wɔ afe aduonu baako mu sɛ ɔsom po a ɛwɔ ɔsom mu no bu akwan a wɔfa so yɛ nyamesom, animuonyam ne nwomasua so. Nokwarem no, Oheneba ankɔ Achimota Sukuu no. Mmom no, wɔde adesua mmoa maa Ghana Amanaman Ntam Sukuu (GIS) denam Atikolo Dunwɔtwe Nwomasoɔ so. GIS alumus William Huckman ne awofoɔ foforɔ baanan na wɔhyehyɛɛ ahotosoɔ no de hyɛɛ nwomasua kwan ne pɛpɛɛpɛyɛ ho nkuran. examples.swap: Ɔne Akansi ga Amammerɛ Agyinatuo foforɔ a wɔdii kan gyaee sɛ wɔbɛkyerɛw wɔn din wɔ Asɛnnibea a ɛwɔ Nokwasɛm gyinapɛn mpem mmienu ne aduonu baako wɔ wɔn awosuo mu nsakraeɛ a emu yɛ den nhyehyɛeɛ no yɛeɛ. According to research, there are five critical times for handwashing with soap: before eating, after defecation, after urination, before holding children, and before preparing food. These times are especially important for mothers and caregivers to reduce the incidence of diarrhoea among children under five.

Yes, research has shown that washing hands with soap ten or more times a day can be time-consuming, which may deter some individuals from practicing regular handwashing. Additionally, the cost of soap and water can also be a burden on household finances, particularly in areas where resources are limited.

According to the study, as few as four percent of mothers engaged in handwashing with soap after defecation, and only two percent after cleaning a child's bottom. These findings highlight the need for improved education and awareness about the importance of handwashing with soap in preventing diarrhoea.

examples.src: **He mentioned that the country needs one hundred,zero housing units annually to bridge the rising housing deficit. Outgone Works and Housing Minister, Samuel Atta Akyea, believes that President Akufo-Addo intends to tackle affordable housing in his second term. Mr. Atta Akyea has also left a working paper to the new Housing Minister to address the rising housing gap situation, which includes leveraging pension funds to create a mortgage regime for workers. According to Samuel Atta Akyea, addressing the issue of affordable housing is crucial for national security. He stated that 'you can never talk about national security without addressing the issue where a man will lay his head.' examples.src: In the year 2024, the nation of Ghana announced that they were beginning to reverse benchmark values at our various ports. When this issue arose, many people's thought was that it would help the prices of goods coming from abroad to come back down. However, on the day they put it in place, journalists and policy advisors reported it with a lack of proper understanding. Ian Sams, who is an official in government operations, indicated that it is the duty of the "independent press" to look into these matters carefully and see if the matter is the truth or just an idea. It was during this time that Emmanuel Nodjo, an expert in trade, stood up and showed that the things they are doing are not appropriate. Nodjo said, "The reversal of the benchmark values is incremental; it is not something that will make the citizenry expect life to become easy." It is the opinion of many listeners that those in the ports are holding onto things that will allow them to deceive the public. If we look at the reports coming from "customs," it is clear that any changes they make do not show any part that will help the small-scale workers. The issues that Ian Sams encouraged led some advisors to stand up and say, "Our press cannot just accept things; they must use their heads and seek the truth." The matter went on until many people started asking, why are they reversing it based on this, but why don't we see any benefits? Nodjo holds the view that this matter is one that the government needs to rethink because port trade and the lives of workers are at stake. It is history that shows that if the citizenry does not have the truth, then the nation will go down.
examples.ref: Ɛwɔ afe 2024 no, ɔman Ghana kyerɛɛ sɛ wɔrehyɛ aseɛ akɔte benchmark values so wɔ yɛn ports ahorow no mu. Asɛm yi baeɛ no, na nnipa pii adwene ne sɛ ɛbɛboa ma nneɛma a efi amannɔne ba no bo bɛsane aba fam. Nanso, ɛda a wɔde sii hɔ no, amanneɛbɔfoɔ ne nsɛm ho akwankyerɛfoɔ de nteaseɛ a ɛnyɛ pɛ na ɛbɔɔ amanneɛ. Ian Sams, a ɔyɛ ɔpanyin wɔ aban dwumadie mu no, kyerɛɛ sɛ ɛyɛ "independent press" no dwumadie sɛ wɔhwɛ nsɛm yi mu yiye, na wɔnhwɛ sɛ asɛm no yɛ nokware anaa ɛyɛ adwene. Ɛwɔ saa bere yi mu na Emmanuel Nodjo, a ɔyɛ ɔbenfoɔ wɔ dwadie ho, gyinaa hɔ kyerɛɛ sɛ nneɛma a wɔreyɛ no mfata. Nodjo kaa sɛ, "Benchmark values no so a wɔate so no yɛ nkakrankakra, ɛnyɛ nea ɛbɛtumi ama ɔmanfoɔ ahwɛ kwan sɛ asetra bɛyɛ mmerɛw. " Ɛyɛ atiefoɔ pii adwene sɛ, wɔn a wɔwɔ ports no mu no kura nneɛma a ɛbɛma wɔatumi adane atoro ama ɔmanfoɔ. Sɛ yɛhwɛ amanneɛbɔ a efi "customs" ba no, ɛda adi sɛ nsakraeɛ biara a wɔyɛ no, ɛnhu ne fa biara a ɛbɛboa nketenkete adwumayɛfoɔ. Nsɛm a Ian Sams hyɛɛ ho nkuran no na ɛma akwankyerɛfoɔ bi bɛgyinaa hɔ kyerɛɛ sɛ, "Yɛn press no ntumi nnye nneɛma ntom kɛkɛ, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ wɔn tirim nneɛma na wɔhwehwɛ nokware no. examples.src: It can reduce risks, make employees feel secure, and eliminate labor turnover. **Training can also enhance the competitive edge of a company by building team spirit between employees and the management team.** According to the article, training can positively impact employee performance by making employees more resourceful and able to make enhanced use of the organization's property, thus reducing waste. Training can also motivate employees to perform at higher levels by giving them a sense of security and involvement in the company's planning process. *The article identifies three main determinants of individual differences in performance: declarative knowledge, procedural knowledge and skill, and motivation.* Declarative knowledge refers to knowledge about facts, principles, objects, etc., while procedural knowledge and skill refer to the ability to apply that knowledge in practice. According to the article, organizational justice perception affects employee performance through its impact on employee attitudes. When employees perceive injustice, they may alter their level of performance to restore justice. Improving justice perceptions can improve productivity and performance.
examples.ref: Ɛtew akwanhyia so, ɛma adwumayɛfo te ahobammɔ nka na ɛkwati adwumayɛfo a wɔbɛsakra wɔn ho. **Ntetee betumi ama adwumakuw bi akansi mu nkɔso ayɛ kɛse denam kuw honhom a ɛbɛma adwumayɛfo ne adwumayɛfo akuw a wɔhwɛ adwuma so no anya nkɔanim so.** Sɛnea yɛaka wɔ asɛm no mu no, ntetee nya adwumayɛfo adwumayɛ so nkɛntɛnso pa denam adwumayɛfo a ɛma wɔyɛ adwumaden na wotumi de adwumakuw no agyapade a wɔatu mpɔn di dwuma no so. examples.src: In 1957, Ghana became the first country in this sub-region to gain its independence. Many people who talk about history remember that this is what encouraged us to agree that we would have our own nation. However, today, many years later, looking at it, we see there are issues we need to talk about. The report available shows that we need to look at new things and focus our minds on education. The policymakers and stakeholders available have many ways they can take to do things that will help the nation move forward. The Founder’s Day issue is a very important matter. Formerly, we remembered those who moved forward, but today, our issues have become "inverse." It seems we are not in sync with our history. We must try to do things that will make our children get the right mindset. If we go to school, we see that the things they teach us have ways they can be used to tell history to our children well. It is not that we should say the same thing, but we must look at how we will do it so it meets what is in us today. In the plans that have been made, they say the guidance available will help us make changes. If our understanding and the things we do do not match, then it will be hard for us to move forward. So, we must focus our minds and seek the appropriate ways we can use to deal with our issues. History is not there for us to play with, but it is there for us to use to teach our children. We must watch what we do and try to do things that will help the nation move forward in all the things that are available. It is not only the things in the report that are important, but the ones we ourselves use to work are even more important. Our country has an amazing history, so we must watch carefully and not let our hands ruin our history. If we do that, we are showing that our ancestors' efforts are of no benefit, and that is also not true. So, we all must try hard.
examples.ref: Wɔ afe 1957 mu no, Ghana bɛyɛɛ ɔman a odii kan wɔ sub-region yi mu a ɛnyaa ne faahodie. Nnipa bebree a wɔka abakɔsɛm no kae sɛ ɛno na ɛhyɛɛ yɛn nkuran ma yɛpenee so sɛ yɛbɛnya yɛn ankasa ɔman. Nanso, nnɛ, mfeɛ bebree a atwam yi, yɛrehwɛ a, yɛhunu sɛ nsɛm bi wɔ hɔ a ɛsɛ sɛ yɛka ho asɛm. Report a ɛwɔ hɔ no ma ɛda adi sɛ ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhwɛ nneɛma foforo na yɛde yɛn adwene kɔ adesua mu. Policymakers ne stakeholders a wɔwɔ hɔ no, wɔwɔ akwan bebree a wɔbɛtumi afa so ayɛ nneɛma a ɛbɛboa ma ɔman no kɔ anim. Founder’s Day asɛm no, ɛyɛ asɛm a ɛho hia paa. Kan no, yɛkae nnipa a wɔkɔɔ anim no, nanso nnɛ, yɛn nsɛm no ayɛ sɛ "inverse". Ɛbɛyɛ sɛ yɛne yɛn abakɔsɛm no mmɔ mu. Ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɔ mmɔden yɛ nneɛma a ɛbɛma yɛn mma anya adwene a ɛfata. Sɛ yɛkɔ sukuu a, yɛnhunu sɛ nneɛma a wɔkyerɛ yɛn no, ɛwɔ akwan a wɔbɛtumi afa so aka abakɔsɛm no kyerɛ yɛn mma yie. Ɛnyɛ sɛ yɛbɛka asɛm no koro no ara, nanso ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhwɛ sɛnea yɛbɛyɛ no ma ɛbɛhyia nea ɛwɔ yɛn mu nnɛ. Wɔ nhyehyɛeɛ a wɔayɛ no mu no, wɔka sɛ akwankyerɛ a ɛwɔ hɔ no bɛboa ma yɛayɛ nsakraeɛ. Sɛ yɛn nteaseɛ ne yɛn nneɛma a yɛyɛ no nhyia a, ɛnde ɛbɛyɛ den sɛ yɛbɛkɔ anim. Nti, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛde yɛn adwene si so na yɛhwehwɛ akwan a ɛfata a yɛbɛtumi afa so adi yɛn nneɛma ho dwuma. Abakɔsɛm no nni hɔ sɛ yɛde bɛdi agorɔ, nanso ɛwɔ hɔ sɛ yɛde bɛkyerɛkyerɛ yɛn mma. Ɛwɔ sɛ yɛhwɛ nea yɛyɛ no, na yɛbɔ mmɔden sɛ yɛbɛyɛ nneɛma a ɛbɛboa ma ɔman no kɔ anim wɔ nneɛma a ɛwɔ hɔ nyinaa mu. Ɛnyɛ nneɛma a ɛwɔ report no mu nko ara na ɛho hia, nanso nea yɛn ankasa yɛde bɛdi dwuma no na ɛho hia kɛse. Yɛn man no wɔ abakɔsɛm a ɛyɛ nwanwa, nti ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhwɛ yie na yɛamfa yɛn nsa anka yɛn abakɔsɛm no mmuagu. Sɛ yɛyɛ saa a, na yɛrekyerɛ sɛ yɛn nananom mmɔdenbɔ no nni mfasoɔ biara, na ɛno nso ɛnyɛ nokware. Nti, yɛn nyinaa ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɔ mmɔden.

examples.src: Mr. Asare, who was the head teacher (official/legal advisor), went on PM Express on JoyNews about how they will discuss the matter. He said the Attorney General's office made a great mistake. *They advised the government to terminate the agreement, but that is what brought great trouble upon this nation.* There is no doubt that the matter is one that troubles the mind. How they told the story, GPGC and Trafigura sued the government for breaching the agreement. It is a frightening thing, because Ghana does not have the money that can pay that debt. **Also, the matter concerning the 15 people they indicated are "failed asylum seekers" and another 11 who come from abroad and have finished their jail time in the UK, it is also a matter that is making people talk.** They placed the matter that it is a "national security" matter. Many people in the parliament asked why the government is bringing these people to Ghana? But the government stood in their place saying it is not any great matter. Mr. Asare pointed his finger at the guides (advisors) that their "ill-advice" is what put Ghana into this great trouble. It is almost as if all the matters show clearly that the government could not think about itself well before they removed those laws.
examples.ref: Mr. Asare a na ɔyɛ kyerɛkyerɛfo panyin no kɔɔ PM Express so wɔ JoyNews sɛdeɛ wɔbɛdi asɛm no ho nkɔmmɔ. Ɔkaeɛ sɛ Attorney General dwumadibea no dii mfomsoɔ kɛseɛ. *Wɔtuu aban foɔ sɛ wɔntwa apam no mu, nanso ɛno na ɛde ɔhaw kɛseɛ baa ɔman yi so.* Akyinnyegyeɛ biara nni ho sɛ, asɛm no yɛ nea ɛhaw adwene. Sɛnea wɔkaa asɛm no, GPGC ne Trafigura bɔɔ aban no ka sɛ wɔatwa apam no mmra so. Ɛyɛ nneɛma a ɛyɛ hu, ɛfiri sɛ Ghana nni sika a ɛbɛtumi atua saa ka no. **Nso, asɛm a ɛfa nnipa 15 a wɔkyerɛɛ sɛ wɔyɛ "failed asylum seekers" ne afoforo 11 a wɔfiri amanɔne na wɔawie n'afiase wɔ UK no nso, ɛyɛ asɛm a ɛrehyɛ amanfoɔ nkɔmmɔ.** Wɔtoo asɛm no sɛ ɛyɛ "national security" asɛm. Mmarahyɛ badwa no mu nnipa pii bisaa sɛ adɛn na aban no de saa nnipa yi ba Ghana? Nanso aban no gyinaa wɔn ananmu sɛ ɛnyɛ asɛm kɛseɛ biara. Ɛkame ayɛ sɛ nsɛm nyinaa da adi sɛ aban no antumi annwene ne ho yie ansa na wɔreyi saa mmarahyɛ no.

examples.src: *The alleged assailant was detained at the scene, but has not yet been formally identified by the authorities.* However, unconfirmed local media reports suggest that the suspect is a seventy-one-year-old writer and political activist. **According to Interior Minister Matus Sutaj Estok, initial information points to a political motivation behind the attack.** Slovak politicians, including the president, have condemned the shooting as an 'attack on democracy'. Defence Minister Robert Kalinak and Interior Minister Matus Sutaj Estok have blamed the spread of hate speech on social media for the shooting and urged citizens not to 'respond to hate with hate'. Additionally, protection will be provided to constitutional officials, journalists, and public figures who could be subject to similar attacks. According to Deputy Prime Minister Tomas Taraba, Prime Minister Robert Fico's procedure in hospital has gone well, and he is not in a life-threatening situation at the moment. However, his presidency has been highly contentious, with thousands of Slovaks protesting against his proposed reform of the public broadcaster in recent weeks.
examples.ref: *Wɔkyeree nea ɔtow hyɛɛ no ​​so no wɔ baabi a asiane no sii no nanso atumfoɔ no nnya nhuu ne din.* Nanso, mpɔtam hɔ nsɛm ho amanneɛbɔfo amanneɛbɔ ahorow a wonsii so dua kyerɛ sɛ nea wosusuw sɛ ɔyɛ ɔkyerɛwfo a wadi mfe aduɔson biako na ɔyɛ amammuisɛm. **Ɔman no mu ɔman soafo Matus Sutaj Istok kae sɛ nsɛm a wodii kan de mae no kyerɛ sɛ amammui adwene bi na ɛde ntua no bae.** Slovakia amammuifo a ɔmampanyin no ka ho kasa tiaa atuo a wɔtotowee no sɛ ‘demokrasi ntua’. Ɔman Bammɔ soafo Robert Kalinak ne Ɔman no mu Ɔsoafo Mats Sutaj Istok kaa ɔtan ho nsɛm a ɛtrɛwee wɔ sohyial media so wɔ tuo a wɔtotowee no akyi ho asɛm na wɔhyɛɛ ɔmanfo nkuran sɛ ‘wɔmfa ɔtan nyɛ wɔn ade wɔ ɔtan ho’. Bio nso, wɔde ahobanbɔ bɛma amansan mmara mu mpanyimfo, nsɛm ho amanneɛbɔfo ne ɔmanfo ananmusifo a ebia wobehyia ntua a ɛte saa ara. Sɛnea Ɔmanpanyin Abadiakyiri Thomas Taraba kyerɛ no, Ɔmanpanyin Robert Fico ayaresa wɔ ayaresabea hɔ no rekɔ so yiye na onni tebea a ɛde ne nkwa to asiane mu mu. Nanso, akyinnyegye kɛse wɔ ɔmampanyin no ɔmampanyin dibea ho, na Slovakiafo mpempem pii kasa tia nsakrae a ɔpɛ sɛ ɔyɛ wɔ baguam amanneɛbɔ mu wɔ nnansa yi adapɛn mu no.
examples.dict: *Wɔakyere obi a wɔkyerɛ sɛ ɔtow hyɛɛ obi so wɔ baabi a asɛm no siiɛ, nanso mpanimfoɔ nnya nhuu no wɔ aban kwan so. Nanso, mpɔtam hɔ nsɛm ho amanneɛbɔfo amanneɛbɔ ahorow a wonsii so dua kyerɛ sɛ nea wɔsusu no yɛ ɔkyerɛwfo a wadi mfe aduɔson biako ne amammui mu akansifo. *Sɛnea Ɔman no mu ɔman soafo Matus Suta Ijistok kyerɛ no, nsɛm a wodii kan de mae no twee adwene sii amammui adwene a ɛwɔ ntua no akyi no so. Slova amammui ananmusifo a ɔmampanyin no ka ho akasa atia tuobɔ no sɛ ntua a wɔde ba bi-ma-menka-mibi amammuo so. Ɔman Bammɔ soafo Robert Kalinak ne Ɔman no mu soafo Matthew Sausta Ijstok de nitan kasa a ɛfa nkitahodie ntentan a wɔde tuo tobɔ ho no ho asodi too ntrɛmu so na wɔhyɛɛ mma sɛ ɛnsɛ sɛ wɔde to ɔtan a ɛwɔ ɔtan mu. The AIB has warned against speculation and stated that they do not rely on unverified data. Acting Commissioner John M. K. Wumborti explained that the bureau does not speculate, but rather investigates and comes out with findings based on verified data. examples.src: *These tests detect the various antigens of the HIV virus and differentiate between the various HIV types.* However, they are more expensive and require sophisticated machinery, making them less accessible in resource-constrained areas. The CD4 count is measured in absolute numbers or by percentage cell count values. The absolute number gives the specific level of immune suppression with age, usually used in adults. The percentage count places an individual in an immunologic category, which is a better marker of identifying disease progression in young children. **For example, CDfour values in healthy infants who are infected are considerably higher than those observed in even uninfected adults and slowly decline to adult values by age six years.** According to experiments performed by Edwards et al in two thousand and one, using isolates of HIV-one, HIV-two and SIV, human cells were successfully infected independent of CD4. This suggests that CD4 is not a prerequisite for entry by these viruses. Additionally, research by Janeway in one thousand, nine hundred and ninety-one and Hugin et al in one thousand, nine hundred and ninety-one found that HIV super antigens may stimulate and trigger massive expansion of CD4+ T cells, killing them in the process. The absolute CD4 + T lymphocyte cell count is used to evaluate the immune status of patients with suspected immune deficiencies. The cell count at a point in time is the desired cellular parameter most closely associated with HIV disease progression and patient prognosis. According to research by Wei et al and Ho et al in one thousand, nine hundred and ninety-five, there is a continuous production of new viruses in HIV infections, resulting in the destruction and replacement of one bitsillion CD4+ cells per day.
examples.ref: *Saa nhwehwɛmu yi kyerɛ HIV mmoawa no antigens ahorow na ɛkyerɛ nsonsonoe a ɛda HIV ahorow ahorow ntam.* Nanso ne bo yɛ den yiye na ehia mfiri a ɛyɛ nwonwa, na ɛma wontumi nkɔ hɔ wɔ mmeae a nneɛma pii nni hɔ. Wɔde dodow a edi mũ susuw CD4 dodow no ho anaasɛ sɛ nkwammoaa dodow no ɔha biara mu nkyem 100. Wɔtaa de dodow a edi mũ no di dwuma wɔ mpanyimfo mu de ma nipadua no mu tumi a ɛko tia nyarewa a ɛfa mfe pɔtee bi ho. Ɔha biara mu nkyem a wɔkan no de ankorankoro bi to nipadua no mu tumi a ɛko tia nyarewa no mu, na ɛno yɛ ade a eye sen biara a wɔde hu sɛnea yare no kɔ so wɔ mmofra nkumaa mu. **Sɛ nhwɛso no, CIDFOR gyinapɛn ahorow a ɛwɔ nkokoaa a wɔwɔ apɔwmuden mu no korɔn kɛse sen nea wohu wɔ mpanyimfo a wonni ɔyare no mu no na ɛso tew nkakrankakra bere a wɔadi mfe asia no.** Wɔ nhwehwɛmu mpem abien ne biako a Edwards ne afoforo yɛe, a wɔde HIV-1, HIV-2, ne SIV dii dwuma mu no, wotumi nyaa nnipa nkwammoaa a CD4 nni mu. Eyi kyerɛ sɛ CD4 nyɛ ade a ɛsɛ sɛ wodi kan yɛ ansa na saa mmoawa yi akɔ mu. Bio nso, nhwehwɛmu bi a Janeway yɛe wɔ 1991 mu ne Hugin ne afoforo. wɔ 1991 mu no kyerɛe sɛ HIV super antigens kunkum CD4+ T nkwammoaa wɔ bere a ɛyɛ adwuma na ɛtrɛw no mu. Wɔde CD4 + T lymphocyte nkwammoaa dodow a edi mũ di dwuma de hwɛ sɛnea ayarefo a wosusuw sɛ nipadua no tumi ko tia nyarewa no tumi ko tia nyarewa. Nkwammoaa dodow yɛ nkwammoaa mu ade a ɛkɔ so bere koro mu a ɛne HIV yare no nkɔso ne ɔyarefo nkɔmhyɛ wɔ abusuabɔ kɛse. Wei ne Ho ne afoforo, wɔ wɔn nhwehwɛmu a wɔyɛe wɔ 1,995 mu no, hui sɛ wɔ HIV yare mmoawa mu no, wɔkɔ so yɛ mmoawa foforo, na ɛma wɔhwere CD4+ nkwammoaa ɔpepepem biako na wɔde si ananmu da biara.
examples.dict: *Saa nsɔhwɛ yi kyerɛ HIV mmoawa no antigens ahorow na ɛkyerɛ nsonsonoe a ɛda HIV ahorow ntam. Nanso, ne bo yɛ den na ɛhwehwɛ mfiri a ɛyɛ nwonwa, na ɛma wontumi nnya pii wɔ mmeae a nneɛma a wɔde di dwuma wɔ hɔ no. Wɔnam dodow a edi mũ anaa nkwammoaa dodow no ara mu nkyem 100 so na ɛsusuw CD4 dodow no. Sɛ nhwɛsoɔ no, CIDFOR gyinapɛn ahorow a ɛwɔ nkokoaa a wɔwɔ apɔwmuden mu no dɔɔso wɔ mfeɛ a wɔde di dwuma wɔ mpanyimfoɔ mu. Wɔ nipadua no mu tumi a ɛko tia nyarewa no mu no, ɔha biara mu nkyem a wɔkan no gyina hɔ ma ankorankoro a wɔwɔ mfeɛ nsia mu, a ɛyɛ ade a eye sen biara a ɛkyerɛ yareɛ nkɔsoɔ wɔ mmofra nketewa mu. *Sɛ nhwɛsoɔ no, wɔde mmoawa a wɔakari afi mu a ɛwɔ HIV-1, ne SIV, nnipa nkwammoaa a wɔde mmoawa a wɔakari afi mu no dii dwuma no tumi nyaa CD4 a wɔde wɔn ho to nnyinasosɛm so nkakrankakra. Eyi kyerɛ sɛ CD4 nsɔhwɛ a Edwards ne afoforo yɛe wɔ afe 2011 mu no nyaa nnipa nkwammoaa a ɛde ne ho.

Sɛnea nhwehwɛmu ahorow a Edward ne ne mfɛfo yɛe wɔ mpem abien ne biako mu kyerɛ no, wɔde HIV-1, HIV-2 ne SIV dii dwuma no, nnipa nkwammoaa nyaa CD4 a ɛde ne ho fii mu. examples.src: **Those they arrested are four bodyguards and one driver. The matter started from the road in Abuakwa, where they say these people arrested a driver and used their strength in a rowdy way to pay them back. The police say the matter occurred when traffic was backed up and those on the road were not standing still, which caused disorder. These people they arrested, they say they are protecting Stonebwoy, but the laws and legal systems we have here in Ghana do not have a place where, because you are a superstar, you are protected so you can attack anyone and do whatever to them. The police have sat down and looked into the matter well. Those they arrested, they have taken them to the police station to question them and see if the matter is exactly as it is. It is the second time such a thing has happened, showing that musicians' friends are having issues on the roads. It is right to say that national laws do not have a place for a big name that will stop them. The government is strictly applying the laws. Stonebwoy has also issued a statement distancing himself from the matter, saying he was not involved, but his people did the work. However, the police have said all the people are employees who work for him. All these are things that make people's minds confused on the road. We are waiting to see what the court will say about the matter. The government has said they will strictly enforce the law so that everyone knows that here in Ghana, the law rules. **There is no one who has strength who can raise their hand and do something that is against the law.** The matter continues in Abuakwa, and many people are waiting to hear what will come of it.**
examples.ref: **Wɔn a wɔkyere wɔn no ne bodyguard anan ne kar kyerɛfoɔ biako. Asɛm no firi kwan a ɛwɔ Abuakwa no so, baabi a wɔka sɛ eyinom akyere kar kyerɛfoɔ bi na wɔde wɔn ahoɔden a ɛyɛ basabasa atua no ka. Police no ka sɛ asɛm no baeɛ bere a akwantuo no retɔ so na ɔkwan no mu nnyina ho de basabasa baeɛ. Eyinom a wɔkyere wɔn no, wɔse wɔyɛ nea wɔbɔ Stonebwoy ho ban, nanso mmra ne mmarahyɛ nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛwɔ Ghana ha no nni nea ɔyɛ superstar nti a wɔbɛbɔ no ban nti na ɔbɛdi obiara na ɔayɛ no adeɛ. Police no atena ase pɛ asɛm no mu yie. Wɔn a wɔkyere wɔn no, wɔde wɔn akɔ police adwumayɛbea sɛ wɔbɛbisa wɔn nsɛm na wɔahwɛ sɛ asɛm no teɛ sɛnea ɛteɛ ankasa. Ɛyɛ adeɛ a ɛtɔ so mmienu a ɛte sɛɛ aba a ɛkyerɛ sɛ nnwontofoɔ nnamfoɔ no wɔ akwan mu asɛm. Ɛsɛ sɛ yɛka sɛ amanmuo mmra nni nea ɔwɔ din a wɔbɛgyae no. Aban no mmiako mmiako de wɔn mmara reto adwuma so. Stonebwoy nso de ɔkasa bi ayi ne ho afiri asɛm no mu sɛ ɔno nni mu nanso ne nkurɔfoɔ na wɔayɛ adwuma no. Nanso police no aka sɛ nnipa no nyinaa yɛ nnwuma a wɔyɛ maa no. Eyinom nyinaa yɛ adeɛ a ɛma nnipa adwene yɛ wɔn basabasa wɔ kwan so. Yɛrehwɛ nea asɛnnikuo no bɛka wɔ asɛm no ho. Aban no aka sɛ wɔbɛto mmara no so den ara ma obiara ahu sɛ Ghana ha, mmra na ɛdi hene. **Obiara nni a ɔwɔ ahoɔden a ɔbɛkyerɛ ne nsa na ɔayɛ adeɛ a ɛnne mmra ne kwan.** Asɛm no kɔ so wɔ Abuakwa, na nnipa pii retwɛn sɛ wɔbɛte nea efi mu bɛba.**

examples.src: **In Adidome, Mr. Agbenyo Michael Friday who is an HIV/AIDS Coordinator gave a talk to people to stand firm and go do an HIV test. This worker said that people shouldn't be afraid that they will find out they have the disease or they are not there, rather it is a path they use to hold onto their lives. He used Jimmy Carter's example. *Carter, the former United States President, when he started his job, things didn't show that they were going well, but when he withdrew, he learned and returned to become someone people blessed.* That is how life and politics are. Mustapha Gbande who is the NDC Deputy General Secretary also continued to give warnings to the public. He said that this year's election or any politics that is going on, if anyone wants to bring violence, they will handle it. It is a matter that is there showing that the public wants peace. Journalists are bearing witness to these things that the nation has various ways where they have no understanding at all, but it is there for us to watch how we will come together. Adidome Government Hospital also used an appropriate way to help people get understanding. All this shows that we are at a place where things are showing that we don't have a path to pass through. If we look at Jimmy Carter's example, it shows that the mistakes you make, it is not a path that you should quit the job and hit the ground, rather it is a path to learn. Mustapha Gbande is also showing that violence has no benefit. People shouldn't break the law. It is history that we are writing today. If we talk about the issues happening in our nation, it is what will help us grow. All these things happening are what show that the nation has life.**

examples.src: For instance, the availability of faecal sludge and organic solid waste is vital for successful production, but quantification and availability of waste can be quite challenging due to factors such as open defecation and lack of waste separation. The disposal of faecal sludge and organic solid waste has significant implications for the business model. For example, most faecal sludge generated in Ghana is dumped off without treatment, and there is no accurate quantitative assessment of total volume of faecal sludge treatment. This highlights the need for policy on the disposal of faecal sludge to be in the domain of the municipal assembly, and for partnerships between the public and private sectors to ensure effective disposal and utilization of raw faecal sludge. Studies have shown that most farmers in Ghana have a positive perception towards the use of co-compost from municipal solid waste, but perceive the cost of co-compost to be expensive. *This highlights the need for low-cost but good quality co-compost to be produced, and the potential for enrolling fortifer as one of the fertilizers used by the government in the subsidized fertilizer programme.* Mechanization of processes such as drying could significantly impact the scale of operation and continuity of production. For example, dependence on sunshine for drying restricts operation during raining seasons, affecting the scale of operation. Opting for mechanized operation, such as using electricity generators, could improve continuity of operation and enable larger-scale production.

On the first of November in the year twenty twenty-one, Parliament got involved in the issue of the General Legal Council denying admission to some candidates who sat the entrance examination to the Ghana School of Law. Specifically, four hundred and ninety-nine students were excluded from the admission list.

Parliament initially addressed this issue through a unanimous resolution, directing the General Legal Council to admit all four hundred and ninety-nine litersLB candidates who were denied admission. However, Inusah Fuseini, the former Ranking Member of the Constitutional, Legal and Parliamentary Affairs Committee of Parliament, believed that this approach was confrontational and that Parliament should have instead invited the General Legal Council to discuss the matter as part of their oversight responsibilities.

examples.src: The four major sectors of ceramics production are indeed structural ceramics, refractories, white wares, and technical ceramics. Structural ceramics include bricks, pipes, floor tiles, and roofing tiles. Refractories include kilns linings, gas fire radiant, steel and glass making crucibles. White wares include tableware, wall tiles, decorative art objects, and sanitary wares, often made from clay, quartz, kaolin, and feldspar. Technical or special ceramics, on the other hand, include tiles used in the space shuttle programme, gas burner nozzles, ballistic protection, nuclear fuel uranium oxide pellets, biomedical implants, jet engine turbine blades, and missile nose cones.

examples.src: Yes, bioceramics such as hydroxyapatite have been developed for medical applications. Hydroxyapatite, the natural mineral component of bone, has been made synthetically from biological and chemical sources and can be formed into ceramic materials. These materials are used in orthopaedic implants, which bond readily to bone and other tissues in the body without rejection or inflammatory reactions. They are also used as fillers for orthopaedic plastic screws to aid in reducing inflammation and increasing absorption of these plastic materials.
examples.ref: Yiw, wɔayɛ bioceramics te sɛ hydroxyapatite de adi dwuma wɔ aduruyɛ mu. examples.src: In the appropriate way, if we look at what happened between Naira Marley and Mohbad, it is something appropriate that we examine ourselves well. At that time, many things were going around on social media. They said there was a chat that showed that Naira Marley showed Mohbad some things that were not good. However, when it reached a point, many people came to ask, is this matter true? It is a story that shows our people do not have the patience we would use to go and look for the basis of truth. It is a journalistic requirement that we search through things well before we speak. Mohbad, who made a lot of music, stole many minds. However, when he died, many matters came into the path. Chat papers that they said were there, many people believed them to be true, but when they searched through them, it was nothing at all. It is something that shows our people have a heart for "misinformation" or deception. Not everything you see on the internet is true. **We must have "media literacy" and know how we will search through things.** History teaches us that if we do not have a foundation, we will judge our neighbors on things that have no basis. We must be people who search for the truth before we lay our hands on things. If it happens that we are thinking about Mohbad's matter, it is not just elections and things that are important, but rather, the truth that is between us.

examples.src: However, the article also notes that Forcipomyia midges are considered the main pollinators of cocoa in Ghana. Aphids were found to be the dominant species, constituting about thirty percent of the overall total of arthropods. Diptera, including cecidomyiid, gall midges, drosophila, and ceratopogonids, were also present, but to a lesser extent. However, it's worth noting that the specimens collected failed to show any pollen on their bodies, suggesting that they may not be significant pollinators. The research article highlights that the breeding substrates or sites of potential pollinators of cocoa has been a subject of great interest to scientists of cocoa pollination. *However, the article does not provide specific information on the breeding substrates of cocoa pollinators in Ghana.* It does suggest that knowledge of these breeding substrates could contribute to sustainable production of cocoa. According to the research article, the cultivated T. cacao may have lost its original attraction system for bees due to many generations of extensive selection by cloning for desired cultivars. This selection process may have led to a reduction in the production of volatile compounds found in the floral oils of T. cacao, making the flowers less attractive to bees.
examples.ref: Nanso, nkyerɛwee no ka sɛ wobu Forsypomia midges sɛ wɔn na wɔma kokoo mu nsuo a ɛyɛ fĩ titire wɔ Ghana. Wohui sɛ aphids na wɔyɛ mmoa titiriw, na wɔyɛ arthropods dodow nyinaa mu ɔha biara mu aduasa. Diptera, cecidomidae, gall midges, a Drosophila ne ceratopogonids ka ho, nanso ɛyɛ kakraa bi. Nanso ɛfata sɛ yɛhyɛ no nsow sɛ nhwɛsode ahorow a wɔaboaboa ano no ankyerɛ pollen aba biara wɔ wɔn nipadua so, na ɛkyerɛ sɛ ɛnyɛ nea ɛda adi sɛ wɔbɛyɛ pollinators atitiriw. Nhwehwɛmu krataa no kyerɛe sɛ na kokoo mu nsu a wɔde gu mu anaa beae a wɔwo no yɛ asɛmti a nyansahufo de wɔn adwene si kokoo mu nsu a wɔde gu mu so kɛse. *Nanso, asɛm no mfa nsɛm pɔtee a ɛfa kokoo pollinators a ɛwɔ Ghana ho mma.* Wɔkyerɛ sɛ awo mu nneɛma yi ho nimdeɛ betumi aboa ma wɔayɛ kokoo a ɛbɛkɔ so atra hɔ daa. Sɛnea nhwehwɛmu krataa no kyerɛ no, ebia T. cacao a wɔadua no ahwere tumi a ɛtwetwe ntɛtea esiane awo ntoatoaso pii a wɔde yɛɛ ntɛtea a wɔayɛ no sɛnea wɔpɛ na wɔpaw ntɛtea ahorow a wɔpɛ nti. Ebia saa kwan a wɔfa so paw nhwiren yi maa nneɛma a ɛyɛ hyew a ɛba kakao nhwiren ngo mu no so tew, na ɛmaa nhwiren no nyɛ nea ntɛtea ani nnye ho kɛse.

examples.src: A team is currently assessing the reports presented by the various committees in the selection process to arrive at the best persons to take up the roles. The delay is a measure to ensure diligence through a rigorous selection process. According to President Akufo-Addo, it's been quite an exhaustive process, and they are trying to arrive at some consensus about the appointments. The delay has raised concerns among the public, as it is affecting operations at the metropolitan, municipal and district levels of administration eight months into President Akufo-Addo's re-election. President Akufo-Addo expressed disappointment in the NDC for pulling out of an agreement to contest in MMDCEs elections, which he believed was an opportunity to take multi-party politics to the local government level. He had initially thought it was time to elect MMDCEs, just as MPs and the President are elected, but the NDC's withdrawal hindered this effort. *The MMDCEs appointment process is part of a larger effort to establish democratic participation in local government.* President Akufo-Addo emphasized the need for a broad national consensus to ensure that political parties do not withdraw from agreements aimed at promoting democratic participation in the election of MMDCEs. This context highlights the importance of cooperation and consensus-building among political stakeholders in Ghana.
examples.ref: Wɔ paw nhyehyɛe no mu no, akuw ahorow rehwɛ amanneɛbɔ ahorow a boayikuw ahorow de ama no mu na wɔrekɔ nnipa a wɔyɛ papa nkyɛn ma wɔadi dwuma no ho dwuma. According to a research article, some common safety management practices used by Ghanaian construction companies include providing personal protective equipment (PPE) to site workers, using safety management as a key performance indicator (KPI), and deploying safety officers to regulate safety implementation on site.

The research article found that the implementation of safety management procedures has several impacts on project performance, including quality performance of construction projects, timely delivery of projects, and reduction in potential construction time loss. In fact, quality performance of construction projects was ranked as one of the most significant impacts of safety management, with a mean record of one point nine eight one eight.

examples.src: In Accra city, the matters regarding petroleum and work involving natural resources took place. The Society of Petroleum Engineers, who also hold their summit and exhibition, hosted this meeting. Dr. Suleiman, who is an expert in this field, invited many people to come and learn what is at the foundation of what we can do in Ghana. The matters regarding what happened on March 14 and 15 concerning England's men and women's Six Nations matches that they are playing against Italy, made it seem like it coincides with our meeting at the right time. Many people came, writers and workers from far and wide, they all stood before them and heard Dr. Suleiman's words. He explained that our nation has many ways we can protect ourselves and grow, but it requires us to lead with knowledge. The exhibition showed many things concerning work, technology we will use, and ways we can make our technology advance. All the people who came there showed great excitement in what they saw. It was something that would make our minds become one, and it showed us that we can work together. March 14 and 15 when they played rugby, it was like they also have their competition, and we also have our competition, which is work and national well-being. As the matters went, it was in it that it was exciting and useful. The people at the SPE showed that they will continue to look for ways they can help Ghana so that our resources can work well. This is what must continue, and if we continue to do so, the victory that is ahead of us is what will come.

examples.src: FDI can indeed impact economic growth. FDI inflows are a source of capital formation and financing, and it is one of the factors affecting the growth of an economy. The increase in the productivity of a host country and hence its competitive advantage may occur due to inward FDI. However, the impact of FDI on economic growth is dependent on the host economy's advancement in technology, the stability of the economy of the host economy, the investment policy of the host country, and how open the country is. Additionally, a nation's institutional characteristics, such as its property rights enforcement and legal system, may influence the extent of FDI inflows and capital formation simultaneously.

## The study found that the application of Fertisoil (FS) resulted in a fifty-three percent increase in nodule dry weight over the control.

1. Additionally, the combined application of FS + BX (Boost Xtra) led to a seventy-two percent increase in nodule dry weight over the control, while FS + N25P30 resulted in a one hundred and eleven percent increase.
2. However, the application of BX and N25Pthirty alone did not significantly increase nodule dry weight relative to the control.
3. The study found that the highest nodule dry weight was produced by FS, which was eighty-eight percent higher than the control treatment.

## Nhwehwɛmu no kyerɛe sɛ Fertisoil (FS) a wɔde dii dwuma no maa nodule dry weight no kɔɔ soro ɔha biara mu aduonum abiɛsa sen nea wɔde dii dwuma no.

1. Bio nso, FS + BX (Boost Xtra) a wɔde dii dwuma bom no maa nodule dry weight kɔɔ soro ɔha biara mu aduɔson abien sen nea wɔde dii dwuma no, bere a FS + N25P30 maa ɔha biara mu ɔha ne du-baako kɔɔ soro.

examples.src:
Yes, there is research on the use of neem oil as a natural pesticide. According to Locke, J., neem oil can be used to lock out spores, and it has been studied for its insecticidal properties. Additionally, Mordue, A.J. and Blackwell, A. researched insect antifeedants, including those found in neem oil, and their effectiveness against certain pests.

According to the research, neem oil has been found to be effective against Callosobruchus maculatus, a pest that can damage cowpeas. Naik, R.L. and Dumbre, R.B. studied the effect of neem oil as a surface protectant against Callosobruchus maculatus on the storability and qualities of cowpea. Their research was published in the Bulletin of Grain Technology, twenty-three: thirty-three-thirty-nine.

examples.src: **Changes in solution conditions, such as a decrease in pH or addition of multivalent metal ions or organic cations, can induce the formation of compact humic aggregates. Neutralization or screening of the charges will not facilitate the penetration of water into the molecule, resulting in the formation of compact, hydrophobic nanospheres. These changes in the colloidal state of humic substances are responsible for the transition of the humic matter from dissolved to disperse state. The overall partition constant for the ligand (KD,L) is calculated as the sum of the partition constants for all forms of metal-bound ligand adsorbed and as aggregate (KD,ML) and the partition constants for all forms of non-metal-bound ligand adsorbed and as aggregate (KD,SL). This includes the partition constants for metal-bound ligand adsorbed (Qa,ML) and as aggregate (Qag,ML), as well as the partition constants for non-metal-bound ligand adsorbed (Qa,SL) and as aggregate (Qag,SL). Trace metals associate with humic substances in terrestrial environments, and their distribution is discussed in terms of the partition of humic substances between the solid and solution phases of the soil-solution system. The transfer of metal-bound humic substance to the solid phase affects the relative proportion of the metal in the phases of the soil system. This association has implications for the understanding of the behavior and fate of trace metals in terrestrial environments.**
examples.ref: **Nsakrae a ɛba wɔ solution tebea mu, te sɛ pH a ɛso tew anaasɛ multivalent metal ions anaa organic cations a wɔde ka ho no betumi ama wɔayɛ compacted humic aggregates. Sɛ wɔma ahoɔdennuru no yɛ nea ɛnyɛ hwee anaasɛ wɔma ɛnyɛ hwee a, ɛmma nsu ntumi nkɔ molecule no mu, na ɛma wonya nanospheres a ɛyɛ ketewaa a ɛnyɛ nsu. Saa nsakrae yi a ɛba wɔ humic nneɛma no colloidal tebea mu no na ɛma humic matter dan fi tebea a apete mu kɔ tebea a apete mu. Total mpaepaemu daa ma ligand (KD, L) ma ahorow nyinaa dade-kyekyere ligand adsorbed ne total (KD, ML) ne mpaapaemu daa ma ahorow nyinaa a ɛnyɛ dade ligand adsorbed ne total (KD, SL). Eyi ne mpaapaemu daa ma dade-kyekyere ligand adsorbed (Qa,ML) ne aggregate (Qag,ML), ne afei nso mpaapaemu daa ma ɛnyɛ dade ligand adsorbed (Qa,SL) ne aggregate (Qag,SL). Trace metals ne humic nneɛma a wohu wɔ asase mu nneɛma a atwa yɛn ho ahyia mu wɔ abusuabɔ, na wɔkyerɛkyerɛ ne kyekyɛ mu wɔ humic nneɛma a wɔkyekyɛ wɔ ade a ɛyɛ den ne solution ntam wɔ asase-aduru nhyehyɛe no mu. Humic nneɛma a wɔde dade akyekyere no a wɔde kɔ ade a ɛyɛ den no mu no nya dade dodow a ɛwɔ asase nhyehyɛe no fã ahorow no mu no so nkɛntɛnso. Saa fekubɔ yi wɔ nkyerɛkyerɛmu wɔ dade ahorow a ɛwɔ asase so nneɛma a atwa yɛn ho ahyia mu no nneyɛe ne nkrabea ho ntease mu.**
examples.dict: *Nsesadeɛ a ɛwɔ solution tebea mu te sɛ multivalent dade ions anaa organic cations nhwɛso te anaa nkaeɛ mu no ma nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛfa compacted humic aggregates ho no yɛ kɛseɛ anaa nhwehwɛmu a wɔyɛ wɔ asodi no ho no mma nsuo nwura mu nkɔ molecule no mu, na ɛnam so ma nhyehyɛeɛ a ɛne sɛ wɔde mulphobic narepheres bɛka abom. Saa nsesaeɛ yi a ɛwɔ humic nnoɔma colloidal tebea mu yi na ɛma humic nneɛma a wɔapete no nsateɛ sɛe ɔman no. Wɔbu ntetewmu a ɛkɔ so daa ma ligand (KD, L) nyinaa sɛ mpaebɔ dodoɔ a ɛfa mpaepaemu daa ho ma dadeɛ dɔla ahodoɔ nyinaa (KD, ML) ne mpaepaemu daa a ɛnyɛ dadeɛ a wɔakyekyere no dɔla ne aggregregate (KD,SL). Eyi ka ho ne mpaepaemu daa a wɔde bɛbɔ lagude (Qa,ML) ne dɔteɛ a ɛnyɛ dadeɛ, Dadeteneten (QS) ne aggaggate (QS).
examples.none: *Nsakrae a ɛba wɔ aduru tebea mu, te sɛ dade a wɔde afrafra anaa nea wɔmfa nnuru nni dwuma pii a ɛso tew no betumi ama wɔde ade a ɛyɛ hyew ayɛ. Boa a wɔde afrafra anaasɛ wɔhwehwɛ mu no mma nsu a ɛkɔ molecule no mu no nyɛ mmerɛw, na ɛma wɔde ade a wɔde hyɛ mu, nsu a wɔde yɛ nsu mu no yɛ adwuma. Saa nsakraeɛ yi a ɛka bom yɛ humic nneɛma no na ɛma immic asɛm no dane fi tebea a wɔapete no mu. Wɔbu ligand (KDL,SL) nkyekyɛmu a ɛkɔ so daa ma dadeɛ a wɔakyekyere no nyinaa (KD,ML) nyinaa sɛ sika a wɔkyekyɛ ma nneɛma a wɔde yɛ liganda ne aggregate (KD,SL) ne bere nyinaa a wɔkyekyɛ ma nneɛma a ɛnyɛ dade a wɔakyekyere no nyinaa. Wɔde dade afrafra a ɛyɛ humic nneɛma a ɛwɔ asase ase nneɛma a atwa yɛn ho ahyia mu no bom, na wɔka sɛnea wɔkyekyɛ no ho asɛm wɔ asase no mu nneɛma a ɛyɛ den ne ano aduru afã horow a ɛyɛ den ntam. examples.src: It was a Saturday morning when reporters showed that a man who has made a name in music has achieved victory that brings honor to himself. This victory shows that he will join people whose names are big like Stonebwoy and Black Sherif. But, the communication in it is not sweet. Kofi who is the owner of the song told reporters that, when he and his group finished the song, he did all he could to call Sarkodie so they would do the video, but any way he takes, it doesn't work. Sarkodie didn't come to accept their call, and that has made an idea come to people that, why is the way so hard? But it is not only music that is an issue in this nation. From the gospel that comes from Top Story, Elder Antwi who is a Member of Parliament explained that, it is not the parliament that has the power to fire Ken Ofori-Atta from his job. He said, the President alone has the executive powers to fire a minister. Elder Antwi showed that their work as Members of Parliament is to bring Ken Ofori-Atta's wrong deeds and things he does not do well to the public so the public will know. He said, their work is to warn why he should not stay on his seat. This issue shows that the nation's things are turning a lot. There is a place where music victory and political issues meet. Reporters say many people feel that there should be change in the nation. Here in Ghana, the issue of who has power and who has progress is a big issue. Today, the public is waiting to see how things will move forward.

examples.src: **The correlation matrix in Table eight shows that some elements are positively correlated, while others are negatively correlated. For example, As, Ca, K, Na, V, and Cu are positively correlated with each other, while Al, La, and Pb are negatively correlated. Additionally, the study found that four principal components (PCs) explain eighty-six point eight of the total variance in the soil dataset. The four PCs extracted from the soil dataset represent distinct patterns of element composition. PCone accounting for forty-six point three five eight of the total variance, is positively correlated with As, Ca, K, Na, V, Cu, Cd, and Co. PC2, explaining twenty point one nine one of the total variance, is correlated primarily with As, Mn, Zn, Pb, Cr, and Ni. PCthree accounting for twelve point eight five three of the total variance, is weighted on Al, La, and Pb, while PCfour accounting for seven point four zero seven of the total variance, is positively correlated with Fe. According to the study, four distinct clusters were identified. Cluster one contains only Al, Cluster two contains Zn, Cr, Pb, Ni, Cd, Co, As, Cu, and La, Cluster three contains Ca, Na, V, Fe, and Mn, and Cluster four hectaress only K as its member.**

Bio nso, nhwehwɛmu no kyerɛe sɛ nneɛma atitiriw anan (PCs) kyerɛkyerɛɛ nsɛntitiriw aduɔwɔtwe nsia awotwe mu wɔ nsakrae a ɛwɔ asase mu nyinaa mu. PC anan a wɔayi afiri asase dataset no mu no gyina hɔ ma nhwɛsoɔ a ɛkyerɛ sɛnea nneɛma nketenkete no te. PCone yɛɛ nsɛntitiriw aduanan nsia abiɛsa anum awotwe wɔ nsonsonoe a ɛwɔ mu nyinaa mu, a ɛne As, Ca, K, Na, V, Cu, Cd ne Co. PCone kyerɛkyerɛɛ nsɛntitiriw aduonu biako akron mu wɔ nsonsonoe no nyinaa mu na ɛne As, Mn, Zn, Pb, Cr, ne Ni wɔ abusuabɔ titiriw. PCThree yɛ dumienu nsɛntitiriw awotwe anum abiɛsa wɔ nsonsonoe nyinaa mu, wɔ Al, La, ne Pb mu, bere a PCfour kyerɛw nsɛntitiriw ason anan zero ason wɔ nsonsonoe nyinaa mu, a ɛne Fe wɔ abusuabɔ pa. Sɛnea nhwehwɛmu no kyerɛ no, wɔkyerɛɛ akuw ahorow anan. Akuo baako no kura Al nko ara, akuakuo mmienu no kura Z, CR, Pb, Ni, Cd, Co, As, Cu, ne La, akuakuo mmiɛnsa no kura Ca, Na, V, Fe, ne Mn, na akuakuo anan no kura K nko ara sɛ ɔmannifoɔ.**
examples.dict: *Ɛpono awotwe abusuabɔ nhyehyɛeɛ no kyerɛ sɛ nkyekyɛmu ahodoɔ bi wɔ abusuabɔ pa, berɛ a nkyekyɛmu ahodoɔ bi wɔ abusuabɔ bɔne. Bio nso, adesua no kyerɛ sɛ nneɛma atitiriw anan (PCs) kyerɛkyerɛ nsonsonoeɛ nyinaa mu pɔ aduɔwɔtwe nsia a ɛwɔ asase mu data mu. examples.src: This approach allowed the researchers to investigate the relationship between financial inclusion and loan accessibility in the Ashanti region of Ghana. The study was carried out in the Ashanti region, which is the second largest and most populous city in Ghana, after the national capital Accra. The region was chosen because it has a varying concentration of financial institutions, with the Suame Municipal having a higher concentration, while Kwabre East and Atwima Kwanwoma have fewer financial institutions. **This variability allowed the researchers to examine the impact of financial inclusion on SMEs accessing credit from financial institutions.** The study found that income, age, education, and engagement status are statistically significantly correlated to the log-odds ratio of using formal credit, while gender is significantly adversely correlated to the log-odds ratio of using only informal credit. *Additionally, the study found that access to finance is a significant constraint to firm growth, and that financing is very important for firm growth.* The study found that informal credit has no statistically significant connection with income, suggesting that credit from informal avenues, such as family and friends, is similarly accessible to all, regardless of income level. This is an important finding, as informal credit is a key source of credit in Africa and other emerging nations.

examples.src: **The study found that the use of manure increased pearl millet yield by twenty-five percent and nutrient uptake by thirty percent compared to the control treatment. The study found that partially acidulated phosphate rocks with high solubility were more effective in improving crop yields than those with low solubility. Additionally, the study found that the iron and aluminum oxide content of phosphate rock can also affect its solubility and agronomic effectiveness. According to a review by Hinsinger in two thousand and one milescroorganisms play a crucial role in phosphate solubilization through various mechanisms, including the production of organic acids, enzymes, and siderophores. **These mechanisms help to solubilize phosphate from mineral sources, making it available to plants.** Additionally, a study by Vassilev et al. in one thousand, nine hundred and ninety-seven found that immobilized Aspergillus niger can solubilize rock phosphate, highlighting the potential of microorganisms in improving phosphate availability to plants. According to a study by Savini et al. in two thousand and sixteen, the long-term application of phosphate rock can have a positive impact on soil fertility and crop yields. Sɛnea Hinzinger nhwehwɛmu no kyerɛ no, mmoawa a wɔwɔ akwansin mpem abien ne biako mu no di dwuma titiriw wɔ phosphate a wɔde hyɛ mu no mu wɔ akwan horow pii so, a nea ɛka ho ne organic acid, enzymes, ne siderophores a wɔyɛ. **Saa akwan yi boa ma phosphate a efi aboɔden abo mu no tew, na ɛma afifide nya bi.** Bio nso, nhwehwɛmu bi a Vassive ne ne mfɛfo yɛe no. Sɛnea nhwehwɛmu a Savini ne ne mfɛfo yɛe kyerɛ no. Wɔ mpem abien ne dunsia mu no, phosphate abotan a wɔde bedi dwuma bere tenten no benya nkɛntɛnso pa wɔ asase no mu nnɔbae ne nnɔbae aba so. Nhwehwɛmu no sii so dua sɛ Minjingu tumi maa atoko ne soyabean aba kɔɔ soro ɔha biara mu aduonu ne dunum, wɔ mfe du mu denam phosphate abo a ɔde guu so no so. examples.src: Each PVC pipe was sealed at the bottom to make it watertight and then drilled at sixty centimeters, one hundred and ten centimeters, and one hundred and seventy-seven point five centimeters from top to bottom to create sampling ports. About fifty centimeters below the middle sampling port was another sampling port, which represented eighty centimeters soil depth. The last sampling port at the bottom had a total of one point five meters soil depth, including the freeboard. The sampling ports were used to collect samples at different depths and times to study the removal efficiency of contaminants as a function of time.
examples.ref: Wɔto PVC paipu biara mu wɔ ase na nsuo ntumi nkɔ mu na afei wɔtu wɔ sɛntimita aduosia, sɛntimita ɔha ne du ne sɛntimita ɔha aduɔson nson nsɛntitiriw anum firi soro kɔ fam. Bɛyɛ sɛntimita aduonum wɔ mfinimfini hyɛn gyinabea a wɔfa nhwɛsode no ase no, na hyɛn gyinabea foforo a wɔfa nhwɛsode no wɔ hɔ, a ɛkyerɛ sɛ asase no mu dɔ yɛ sɛntimita aduɔwɔtwe. Na hyɛn gyinabea a etwa to a wɔfaa nhwɛsode no ase no, na asase no mu dɔ nyinaa yɛ beae biako mita anum, a freeboard no ka ho. Wɔde nhwɛsodeɛ hyɛn gyinabea di dwuma de boaboa nhwɛsoɔ ano wɔ bun ne mmerɛ ahodoɔ mu de sua efĩ a wɔyi firi hɔ yie wɔ berɛ mu.
examples.dict: Wɔsɔɔ PVC paipu biara hwɛe wɔ ase hɔ na ama ayɛ nea eye sen biara a hwee nni mu, kilomita ɔha ne du, ne ɔpɛ a ɛyɛ sɛntimita anum kosi aduɔson ason, na ɛyɛɛ nhwɛsodeɛ hyɛn gyinabea. examples.src: In the month of December, the Ghana government and the Forestry Commission did work that will make our people breathe. Those whose job is to look after the forest and the things in it reported that they have won in the "red-zoned" forest reserves that are in our nation. If we look at the issues concerning Abore, Miradani North, Nkran, and Esaase, it was a very worrying issue. These areas are areas where they have taken permission to work in, but some people who are not following the law let their guard down and went to spoil those areas. DCOP Teye-Cudjoe, who is a senior police officer, put his hand to the work that they will search for those behind these evil actions and bring them before the law. He said, "We have started investigations, and I give you assurance that we will pray/hunt for them and catch those behind these actions." The minister in charge of this matter also said, they have joined with the Forestry Commission, and through those animals (scouts/guards), they have gotten all the areas they call 'red-zoned' reserves out of the hands that shouldn't be there. The people who have lived in these areas for many years were happy that the government fixed the matter. However, history shows that these actions are common, and it is our people who must ensure it doesn't return again. It’s not just to say they have caught them, but we must see that the law is there for everyone. Today, when the Forestry Commission and police have finished their work, we look forward to these areas being things that will make our nation have progress. It is history that shows that if the government and the people join forces, we can save our forest and our land from the hands of those who want to destroy it.
examples.ref: Ɔpɛnimaa bosome no, Ghana aban ne Forestry Commission dii dwuma a ɛbɛma yɛn nkurɔfoɔ ahome ka. Wɔn a wɔn adwuma ne sɛ wɔbɛhwɛ kwaeɛ ne nneɛma a ɛwɔ mu no bɔɔ amanneɛ sɛ, wɔadi nkonim wɔ "red-zoned" forest reserves a ɛwɔ yɛn man mu no. Sɛ yɛhwɛ nsɛm a ɛfa Abore, Miradani North, Nkran, ne Esaase ho a, na ɛyɛ asɛm a ɛhaw adwene pa ara. Saa mmeaeɛ yi, ɛyɛ mmeaeɛ a wɔagye ho kwan sɛ wɔdi mu dwuma, nanso nnipa bi a wɔnni mmara mu gyae wɔn ani kɔsɛee saa mmeaeɛ no. DCOP Teye-Cudjoe, a ɔyɛ polisifoɔ panyin, de ne nsa hyɛɛ aseɛ sɛ wɔrebɛhwehwɛ wɔn a wɔwɔ saa nneyɛɛ bɔne yi akyi na wɔde wɔn aba mmara anim. Ɔkaa sɛ, "Yɛafiri nhwehwɛmu ase, na me ma wo awerɛhyem sɛ yɛbɛbɔ wɔn mpaeɛ na yɛakyere wɔn a wɔdi saa nneyɛɛ yi akyi. " Ɔsoafoɔ a ɔhwɛ saa asɛm yi so nso kaeɛ sɛ, wɔne Forestry Commission abɔ mu, na wɔnam saa mmoa no so, wɔanya saa mmeaeɛ a wɔfrɛ no 'red-zoned' reserves no nyinaa afiri nsa a ɛnsɛ sɛ ɛwɔ mu. Nnipa a wɔte mmeaeɛ yi mfeɛ bebree no ani bɛgyee wɔn sɛ aban no asiesie asɛm no. Nanso, abakɔsɛm kyerɛ sɛ saa nneyɛɛ yi yɛ nea ɛtaa ba, na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛn manfoɔ na wɔhwɛ sɛ ɛrensane nni hɔ bio. Ɛnyɛ sɛ yɛbɛka sɛ wɔakye wɔn pɛ, nanso ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhunu sɛ mmara no wɔ hɔ ma obiara. In Ghanaian folktales, the setting often refers to the place or location where the story takes place. Traditionally, folktales were told in the home, particularly in the evening, and were meant to cater to children and women who were confined to the house. However, folktales were also told in public places such as funerals and traditional festivals.

With the advent of Westernization, folktales have moved from oral traditions to written literature, starting from the beginning of the twentieth century. This shift was partly due to the efforts of national bodies of writers, such as in Kenya, which developed materials in indigenous languages for adoption in schools. In the 1950s and 1960s, many folktales were written down to serve as reading materials for school children.

Yes, folktales are believed to be a non-human resource of communal society that helps to bring up children. They are used to train children for good morals and to pass on traditions, norms, and values of society to the younger generation. Folktales also reflect the physical and socio-cultural environment of the community, and their performance brings out the actions, behavior, and words of the characters, which helps to socialize children.

The 'Ananse' stories are a type of trickster tale, where the main character uses tricks to survive or reign supreme. These stories are very popular among the Akan people of Ghana, and they have been retold and published in various forms, including books and television shows. The stories are significant because they teach moral lessons and promote virtues such as kindness and fairness.

examples.src: Cowpea, also known as Vigna unguiculata L. Walp., is an annual legume that originated in Africa. It's divided into three groups based on morphological characteristics: Vigna unguiculata, Vigna sesquipedalis, and Vigna sinensis. Cowpea is a warm-season, annual, herbaceous legume with a growth habit that ranges from indeterminate to fairly determinate.
examples.ref: Nantwi a wɔfrɛ no Vigna unguiculata L. Walp nso. Wɔsan frɛ no, yɛ afe afe atoko a efi Afrika. Wɔakyekyɛ wɔn mu akuo mmiɛnsa a egyina wɔn nsɛsoɔ su so: Vigna unguiculata, Vigna sesquipedalis ne Vigna sinensis. Cowpea yɛ bere a ɛyɛ hyew, afe afe, nhabannuru a ɛyɛ nhabannuru a ne nyin su fi nea wontumi nhu so kosi nea ɛyɛ pintinn yiye.

examples.src: The research states that cowpea responds positively to irrigation, but will also produce well under dryland conditions. However, if irrigation is used, more vegetative growth and some delay in maturity may result. The most critical moisture requiring period is just prior to and during bloom. It's essential to ensure that the crop is not overwatered, especially in more northern latitudes, as this can suppress growth by lowering soil temperatures.

examples.src: As the election rain falls, the whole nation's eyes are on the security agencies. The Ghana Armed Forces and other bodies they work with have started sending reinforcement teams to regions with risks. Their primary work is to ensure that the "integrity" of the election is not marred by anything. The security agencies give us an "unambiguous message" that their mind is not set on any chaos or "malpractice." Their actions show that they are ready to protect everyone, and show criminals that they have no room. The matter is work they have led so that the election will proceed well. In the first place, they have sent many workers to places where issues could arise. All this shows that the government does not ignore things that will cover the election. Parliamentarians and political parties have also said they will try to ensure their followers stay calm. But what is important is that everyone watches over themselves. The message we have heard is that these "reinforcement teams" are not there to cause chaos, but rather they will protect the election. Some things happening abroad show that the security is prepared to take "measures" to ensure peace remains. These are things relating to "safeguarding the electoral process." Some of our people have spoken on this issue, and they all say that we all must join in. Today, if you are someone who works with clients, you must give them "support." Many clients fear that the election will turn chaotic, but the security's explanations give us assurance. The Ghana Armed Forces' work is a hard one, and we all must give them our "cooperation." If everyone does their part, it will be easy for the election to proceed well. Right now, the "security posture" in the nation shows that the nation is not there for wickedness. That is why, let's not let our hands shake; let us cast our vote and go home.

examples.src:
Ghana has indeed been a leader in mobile technology adoption in Africa. In one thousand, nine hundred and ninety-two gramshana became the first Sub-Saharan African country to launch cellular mobile services. By January two thousand and thirteen gramshana had achieved the highest mobile broadband penetration in Africa, according to the International Telecommunications Union. However, it's worth noting that the high mobile penetration rate is partly due to the phenomenon of individuals holding multiple phone chips, rather than every Ghanaian having a mobile phone.

The UTAUTtwo metersodel was adapted for research in Ghana by integrating hedonic motivation, price value, and habit into the original UTAUT model. The adapted model included eight variables, which were later reduced to four: performance expectancy, effort expectancy, facilitating conditions, and ICT. These variables were used to assess consumer adoption of technology in Ghana.
examples.ref:
Ghana di anim ampa wɔ mobile mfiridwuma a wɔde di dwuma wɔ Afrika no mu. Wɔ afe 1992 mu no, Gramhana Cellular bɛyɛɛ ɔman a edi kan a ɛwɔ Sahara anafo fam a ɛde telefon so dwumadi sii hɔ. Wɔ January 2013 mu no, Gramhana na ɛkyerɛw mobile broadband server dodow a ɛsen biara wɔ Afrika, sɛnea Amanaman Ntam Telecommunication Union kyerɛ no. Nanso, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhyɛ no nsow sɛ telefon a wokura kyin a ɛkɔ soro no fã bi fi adeyɛ a ɛne sɛ ankorankoro wɔ telefon chips pii sen Ghanani biara a ɔwɔ telefon a wokura kyin.

Wɔyɛɛ UTAUTtwo Meters nhwɛsoɔ no maa nhwehwɛmu wɔ Ghana denam hedonic motivation, value, ne suban a wɔde kaa UTAUT model mfitiaseɛ no ho no so. Nhwɛsoɔ a wɔayɛ mu nsakraeɛ no de nneɛma awotwe a ɛsakra ka ho, a akyiri yi wɔtew so kɔɔ anan: bere tenten a wɔde yɛ adwuma, mmɔdenbɔ a wɔhwɛ kwan, nneɛma a ɛma ɛyɛ mmerɛw, ne ICT. Wɔde saa nsakraeɛ yi dii dwuma de hwɛɛ adetɔfoɔ mfiridwuma a wɔde di dwuma wɔ Ghana.

Ghana ayɛ ɔkannifoɔ wɔ mobile mfiridwuma a wɔde di dwuma wɔ Abibiman no mu. Wɔ Ɔpɛpɔn 2013 mu no, gramhana nyaa mobile broadbrand server dodow a ɛsen biara wɔ Abibiman, sɛnea Amanaman Ntam Telecommunication Union kyerɛ no. Nanso, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛhyɛ no nsow sɛ telefon a wokura kyin a ɛkɔ soro no fã bi fi nneɛma a ɛsisi a ankorankoro a wɔwɔ telefon chips pii sen sɛ Ghana benya atitiriwfoɔ.

Nea ɛka nhwɛsoɔ a wɔayɛ mu nsakraeɛ no ho ne nneɛma a ɛsesa awotwe, a akyiri yi wɔatew so akɔ anan: dwumadie ho anidasoɔ, mmɔdenbɔ anidasoɔ, tebea a ɛyɛ mmerɛ, ne ICT. Wɔde saa nneɛma a ɛsakra yi dii dwuma de hwɛɛ adetɔfoɔ mfiridwuma a wɔde di dwuma wɔ mfiridwuma ho wɔ Ghana.
